projects.name: Scorka
projects.tagline: Local cricket, scored ball by ball
projects.description: Most local cricket in Pakistan is still scored on paper, so players have no records, rankings or live scores. Scorka lets anyone score a match ball by ball on their phone, run tournaments and build a player record over time.

stats.label: QA test cases in release testing

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Local cricket is played every weekend in towns and villages across Pakistan, but it is scored in notebooks. Scores get lost, tournaments are organised over WhatsApp, and a good player has nothing to show for years of matches.

sections.title: What I built
sections.body: I designed the database and built the whole backend: a Spring Boot REST API behind an Android app.
points: Ball-by-ball scoring: scorecards, run rates and bowling figures come from the record of every ball.
Tournaments with teams, fixtures and live points tables.
Player rankings by village and district, built from match data.
Phone-number login with OTP over SMS, and JWT authentication.
Teams, invites, join requests and in-app notifications.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.body: The Android app (React Native) talks to a Spring Boot API. MySQL stores matches down to every ball, Redis holds short-lived data such as login codes, and Nginx sits in front of the API and serves the website.

sections.title: A security flaw I caught
sections.body: A first design for team join requests stored them in the same table as captain invites. Because invites are accepted by the invited player, a player could have accepted their own request and joined any team. I moved join requests to their own table, let only the captain accept them, and covered every case with tests before release.

sections.title: Quality and shipping
points: 519 automated backend tests.
An independent QA engineer ran 153 test cases on a real device: the scoring maths was verified ball by ball and the app had 0 crashes.
Running in production on a Linux server, with verified Android App Links so shared scorecards open straight in the app.
Released to testers on Google Play.

sections.title: Team
sections.body: I own the backend, database, server and deployment. The mobile app was built with my partner Fahad.
